1	# Structural BPMN (what the registry does not emit)
2	
3	The registry's `xmlTemplate`s give you the `uipath:*` payload for each node
4	(see [registry-workflow.md](registry-workflow.md)). They do **not** give you the
5	structural BPMN that holds those nodes together. This file is the ground truth
6	for everything you author by hand around the templates.
7	
8	Two sources define the contract:
9	
10	- the registry spec `bpmn-spec.json` — enumerates which BPMN element types and
11	  event definitions exist, via its `bpmnElements` section;
12	- the Studio Web canvas serializer
13	  (`PO.Frontend/src/services/serialization/`) — defines how that XML must be
14	  shaped to import and round-trip.
15	
16	Where the registry stops, the canvas serializer is authoritative. Each
17	gap below is labelled **REGISTRY GAP** — the registry exposes no template for
18	it, so author it from this reference.
19	
20	BPMN XML element names are case-sensitive. Use the exact lower-camel BPMN tag
21	names the serializer emits, such as `<bpmn:startEvent>`,
22	`<bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>`, `<bpmn:scriptTask>`, and `<bpmn:endEvent>`.
23	Do not use PascalCase variants like `<bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent>`; XML accepts
24	them syntactically, but BPMN tools do not treat them as the same elements.
25	
26	## The document scaffold (REGISTRY GAP)
27	
28	The registry emits no `<bpmn:definitions>` / `<bpmn:process>` root and no
29	namespace declarations. Author this shell yourself. The canvas import detector
30	(`exporter.ts`) requires: a root `<…:definitions>` carrying a BPMN-spec
31	namespace, at least one `<bpmn:process>`, and (to render) a
32	`<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>`.
33	
34	```xml
35	<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
36	<bpmn:definitions
37	    xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
38	    xmlns:bpmndi="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI"
39	    xmlns:dc="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DC"
40	    xmlns:di="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DI"
41	    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
42	    xmlns:uipath="http://uipath.org/schema/bpmn"
43	    id="Definitions_1" targetNamespace="http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn"
44	    exporter="UiPath (https://bpmn.uipath.com)" exporterVersion="1.0">
45	  <bpmn:process id="Process_1" isExecutable="true">
46	    <!-- variables, flow nodes, sequence flows -->
47	  </bpmn:process>
48	  <bpmndi:BPMNDiagram id="Diagram_1">
49	    <bpmndi:BPMNPlane id="Plane_1" bpmnElement="Process_1">
50	      <!-- one BPMNShape per node, one BPMNEdge per flow -->
51	    </bpmndi:BPMNPlane>
52	  </bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>
53	</bpmn:definitions>
54	```
55	
56	The `uipath:` namespace URI is exactly `http://uipath.org/schema/bpmn`. All
57	`uipath:*` tags inside `extensionElements` are lower-camelCase
58	(`uipath:activity`, `uipath:variables`, `uipath:loopCharacteristics`, …).
59	
60	Every `uipath:activity` / `uipath:event` / `uipath:mapping` carries its node
61	type as a **child** element — `<uipath:type value="<Type>" version="v1" />` —
62	never as a `type=` attribute on the wrapper. This holds both for templated nodes
63	and for any shell you author or preserve by hand.
64	
65	XML comments must not contain `--` (double-hyphen): it is invalid XML and the
66	file will fail to parse. Never paste CLI commands or flags
67	(`--output`, `--connection-id`) into `<!-- … -->`. Keep comments minimal.
68	
69	## A complete minimal file (author from this, not from examples)
70	
71	This is the whole shape — variables, an entry point, one node, a branch, and
72	the diagram — in one valid file. Author from this skeleton plus the registry
73	templates for your nodes. **Do not reverse-engineer the pattern from full

138	
139	## Variables (`BPMN.Variables`)
140	
141	Declare root variables with the `BPMN.Variables` registry template attached to
142	the process via `extensionElements`, or use the canvas `<uipath:variables>`
143	block directly. Variable bodies are CDATA. Reference variables in expressions as
144	`vars.<id>` — see [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
145	Sub-process-scoped variables go in that sub-process's own `<uipath:variables>`.
146	For a value produced only by a task output, prefer root
147	`<uipath:output id="..." name="..." type="..." />`; preserve the exact id and
148	target that same id from `uipath:output var="..."`.
149	
150	## Script tasks (`BPMN.ScriptTask`) — Jint runtime contract
151	
152	`bpmn:scriptTask scriptFormat="JavaScript"` runs under **Jint**, not Node.js or
153	a browser. The mapping payload comes from the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry
154	template, but the runtime contract is fixed:
155	
156	- Only these helpers exist: `uipath.aggregate`, `uipath._aggregate`,
157	  `uipath._pipe`, and a no-op `console`. No npm packages, filesystem, network,
158	  browser globals, or long-running async behavior. Execution envelope is ~64 MB
159	  / 30 s.
160	- Set `uipath:scriptVersion value="v3"` for new scripts; preserve an imported
161	  `value="v2"`. For v2+ the script returns JSON under `response`.
162	- Mapped `args` fields are read as **top-level identifiers** in the script body
163	  (`amount`, not `args.amount`); the input mapping itself stays `name="args"`
164	  with `type="json"` and `target="bodyField"`, and maps each field by variable
165	  id (`=vars.Var_Amount`). Include `<uipath:input name="args" type="json"
166	  target="bodyField"><![CDATA[{}]]></uipath:input>` even when there are no
167	  inputs; this is part of the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry template.
168	- Map the returned object's property back through `source="=result.response"`
169	  (the conventional scalar property) or `source="=result.response.<field>"`
170	  (another object field); `var` points at a declared variable id (do not put the
171	  target id in `name`).
172	- When the output mapping uses `source="=result.response"`, return an object
173	  with a `response` property, such as `return { response: 6 * 7 };`. Do not
174	  return the bare primitive `42` for that mapping shape; there is no
175	  `response` property to bind, so the runtime variable stays empty.
176	- Do not use `source="=result"` with a bare scalar return in live debug/runtime
177	  BPMN. Studio Web can report `FinalStatus: Completed` while the target root
178	  variable still reads back as `{}` or `null` from
179	  `debug-instance variables-all`.
180	- For live debug/runtime runs, never use `source="=this.result"` or
181	  `<uipath:type value="BPMN.Variables" ...>` on a script task output mapping.
182	  That older structural-test shape can pass local validation but leaves root
183	  variables `null` or faults in Studio Web. Use the `BPMN.ScriptTask` mapping
184	  with `source="=result.response"`.
185	- Do not mutate `Globals.*`, `vars.*`, or process variables inside the script
186	  body. The supported path is: return a value from the script, then use a
187	  `uipath:output` mapping to write it to the declared variable. Direct mutation
188	  is not applied to the runtime, so the variable reads empty afterward.
189	
190	```xml
191	<bpmn:scriptTask id="Task_RiskScore" name="Risk Score" scriptFormat="JavaScript">
192	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
193	    <uipath:scriptVersion value="v3" />
194	    <uipath:mapping version="v1">
195	      <uipath:type value="BPMN.ScriptTask" version="v1" />
196	      <uipath:input name="args" type="json" target="bodyField"><![CDATA[{"amount":"=vars.Var_Amount","daysOverdue":"=vars.Var_DaysOverdue"}]]></uipath:input>
197	      <uipath:output name="riskScore" type="number" var="Var_RiskScore" source="=result.response" />
198	    </uipath:mapping>
199	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
200	  <bpmn:script><![CDATA[
201	var score = amount * 0.01 + daysOverdue * 2;
202	return { response: score };
203	]]></bpmn:script>
204	</bpmn:scriptTask>
205	```
206	
207	## Sequence flows, conditions, and gateway defaults (REGISTRY GAP)
208	
209	The registry never emits `<bpmn:sequenceFlow>`, conditions, or the gateway
210	`default` attribute. Author all of them.
211	
212	- A flow: `<bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="A" targetRef="B" />`. The
213	  source/target nodes must also list `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>`
214	  (the registry templates leave `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` placeholders
215	  for exactly these).
216	- Conditional flow body: `<bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_X == "approved"</bpmn:conditionExpression>`.
217	  The canvas normalizes the body to start with `=` — always lead with `=`.
218	- Gateway default flow: set `default="Flow_else"` on the gateway element, and
219	  give that flow no condition.
220	
221	## Gateways
222	
223	Author these gateway types for new BPMN: `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`,
224	`bpmn:ParallelGateway`, `bpmn:InclusiveGateway`, `bpmn:EventBasedGateway`.
225	`bpmn:ComplexGateway` round-trips structurally but is **preserve-only** — do not
226	generate it for new authoring (see [Do not generate for new

### Boundary events (REGISTRY GAP for `attachedToRef` / `cancelActivity`)

A boundary event attaches to an activity and catches an event on it. The
registry exposes no boundary template; author it:

```xml
<bpmn:boundaryEvent id="Boundary_Timeout" attachedToRef="Task_DoWork" cancelActivity="true">
  <bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
    <bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT15M</bpmn:timeDuration>
  </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
  <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OnTimeout</bpmn:outgoing>
</bpmn:boundaryEvent>
```

- `attachedToRef` = id of the activity it sits on. The boundary event and that
  activity must be `flowElements` of the same parent scope.
- `cancelActivity="true"` = interrupting (default); `cancelActivity="false"` =
  non-interrupting. Per the spec, non-interrupting is available for
  Message/Timer/Escalation/Conditional/Signal — **not** Error or Compensate.
- Only one catch-all (no `errorRef`) error boundary event per task, and no two
  error boundary events with the same error code on one task
  (`MULTIPLE_CATCH_ALL_BOUNDARY_EVENTS_ON_TASK`,
  `DUPLICATE_ERROR_BOUNDARY_EVENT_ON_TASK`).

### Retry and error mapping (REGISTRY GAP)

UiPath-specific retry and error-mapping metadata live inside an activity's
`extensionElements`. The error **code** lives on the declared
`bpmn:error errorCode="…"`; `uipath:*` elements reference it through `errorRef`.

```xml
<uipath:retry maxRetryCount="2" retryBackoff="PT30S" retryBackoffType="exponential"
              maxDuration="PT5M" exponentialBase="2" retryAllErrors="false">
  <uipath:errorDefinition errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable" />
</uipath:retry>
<uipath:errorMapping version="v1">
  <uipath:error id="Mapped_ServiceUnavailable" errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable"
                priority="1" condition="=vars.error.code == "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE""
                detail="Service unavailable" retryable="true" />
</uipath:errorMapping>
```

- `uipath:retry` attributes: `maxRetryCount`, `retryBackoff`, `retryBackoffType`,
  `maxDuration`, `exponentialBase`, `retryAllErrors`. Do not use stale aliases
  (`maxAttempts`, `interval`).
- `uipath:error` (mapping) fields: `id`, `errorRef`, `priority`, `condition`,
  `detail`, `retryable` (`true`/`false`). Conditions read the runtime error via
  `vars.error` and contain no assignments. Do not put `code=` on `uipath:error`;
  model the code on `bpmn:error errorCode` and reference via `errorRef`.

## Subprocess, call activity, event subprocess (REGISTRY GAP for structure)

- **SubProcess** (`bpmn:SubProcess`): a container with its own nested
  `flowElements` (start event, nodes, end event) and its own scoped
  `<uipath:variables>`. Variants: `collapsed`, `expanded`, `eventSubprocess`.
  The shape carries `isExpanded` for the collapsed/expanded distinction.
- **Event subprocess**: a `bpmn:SubProcess` with `triggeredByEvent="true"`. It
  must have **exactly one** start event, and that start event **must carry an
  event definition** (with `isInterrupting`) — a blank start event is invalid for
  an event subprocess.
- **Call activity** (`bpmn:CallActivity`): invokes a *separate* Maestro
  instance. The registry provides the `uipath:activity` payload for the
  Orchestrator agentic/case-management call-activity types
  (`Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess[Async]`, `…CaseMgmtProcess[Async]`). A
  plain BPMN `calledElement` round-trips but is not specially authored by the
  canvas layer.
- Each scope (process or sub-process) may have at most one blank (untyped) start
  event (`MULTIPLE_BLANK_START_EVENTS`).

> SubProcess scopes operations *within the same instance*; CallActivity invokes
> a *separate* Maestro instance. Do not conflate them.

## Multi-instance / loop characteristics (REGISTRY GAP — canvas supports it)

The registry spec enumerates **no** multi-instance or loop markers
(`grep` for `multiInstance`/`loopCharacteristics` in `bpmn-spec.json` returns
nothing). This is a genuine registry gap. The Studio Web canvas, however, **does**
serialize them (`elements/nodes.ts`), so author them from the canvas contract:

```xml
<bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics isSequential="true">
  <bpmn:completionCondition xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_Done</bpmn:completionCondition>
  <bpmn:extensionElements>
    <uipath:loopCharacteristics
        inputCollection="=vars.Var_Items" inputElement="item" />
  </bpmn:extensionElements>
</bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics>
```

- `isSequential="true"` = one at a time; `false` = parallel.
- The collection/item binding lives in the `uipath:loopCharacteristics`
  extension (`inputCollection`, `inputElement`), **not** in `loopCardinality`
  (the canvas never reads `loopCardinality`).
- The loop element **must declare `inputElement`** — do not rely on reading a
  bare `iterator`/`iterator.item` downstream without it. For a multi-instance
  **subprocess** body, bind `inputElement="iterator[0]"` on
  `uipath:loopCharacteristics` and pass the current item into body activities
  with `=iterator[0].item`. Do not assume a bare alias such as `=currentItem` is
  in scope inside a marker subprocess body unless the file already uses it.
- Inside the body, read the current item with the `iterator` namespace — see
  [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
- `bpmn:standardLoopCharacteristics` is also recognized (no uipath extension).

Because the registry exposes no template for this, treat it as a documented
authoring path backed by the canvas serializer, and tell the user it is a
registry gap if they ask why no `registry get` covers it.

## Diagram interchange — `bpmndi` (REGISTRY GAP — always generated)

The registry emits no diagram. Import is **diagram-driven**: the canvas builds
nodes from `BPMNShape`s and edges from `BPMNEdge`s, not by walking
`flowElements`. **A node with no shape is invisible; a flow with no edge is
dropped.** Generate the full `BPMNDiagram` with `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`.

- One `<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_<nodeId>" bpmnElement="<nodeId>">` per node, with
  `<dc:Bounds x= y= width= height= />`. SubProcess shapes carry `isExpanded`.
- One `<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_<flowId>" bpmnElement="<flowId>">` per
  sequence flow, with `<di:waypoint x= y= />` points.
- Lay nodes out left-to-right with non-overlapping bounds. Typical sizes: tasks
  100×80, events 36×36, gateways 50×50.

Example:

```xml
<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_StartEvent_1" bpmnElement="StartEvent_1">
  <dc:Bounds x="160" y="100" width="36" height="36" />
</bpmndi:BPMNShape>
<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_Flow_1" bpmnElement="Flow_1">
  <di:waypoint x="196" y="118" />
  <di:waypoint x="260" y="118" />
</bpmndi:BPMNEdge>
```

## Editing operations

Safe, surgical edits on an existing `.bpmn` (preserve content you did not author
— see [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#editing-an-existing-bpmn-preserve-what-you-did-not-author)):

- **Add / delete / reconnect a node**: add the element with a stable id and its
  `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>` refs, add the sequence-flow elements in the
  owning scope. On delete, remove orphaned flows and recheck entry-point variables,
  output mappings, and binding references. Then regenerate the diagram:
  `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`. If CLI unavailable: add/update `BPMNShape`
  and edge waypoints manually.
- **Insert a gateway**: split the existing sequence flow into an incoming and an
  outgoing flow, add conditions to the outgoing flows plus one `default`, add a
  matching join only if branches actually need synchronization. Then regenerate the
  diagram: `uip maestro bpmn format <file.bpmn>`. If CLI unavailable: re-waypoint
  manually (gateway shape + all edges).
- **Move logic into a subprocess**: move only elements that share a valid scope,
  re-scope their variables, recreate legal subprocess flow boundaries, and add a
  second diagram plane for the subprocess so nested content renders.
- **Add an entry point**: use a root-level start event, add a stable unique
  `uipath:entryPointId`, and declare input/output variables whose `elementId`
  matches that start event.

Do not patch generated JSON to fix source behavior — change the `.bpmn` and
regenerate. For `Intsvc.*` activities/triggers, hand editing to CLI enrichment.

### Edit red-flags

Re-check after any edit:

- A diagram plane references a missing process, collaboration, or subprocess.
- A rendered element lacks a shape or its flow lacks an edge/waypoint.
- An entry-point variable points at the wrong start event.
- A `uipath:context` value references a missing binding.
- A topology edit rewrote unrelated `uipath:*` extension XML.
- An Integration Service element carries hand-authored connection details.
